paper.title_en: AI-Sono: A Lightweight Quantum-Inspired Extreme Learning Framework for Screening-Oriented Lung Sound Classification
paper.abstract_en: Respiratory diseases remain a major global health burden, particularly in low-resource settings where access to specialized diagnostic support remains limited. In this context, automated lung sound analysis has emerged as a promising direction for accessible and cost-effective respiratory screening. This paper proposes AI-Sono, a lightweight framework for screening-oriented lung sound Classification based on an Emulated Quantum-Inspired Extreme Learning Machine (EQELM). The proposed method combines respiratory cycle preprocessing, compact acoustic feature extraction, a classically emulated quantum-inspired oscillatory transformation, and analytical Classification through an Extreme Learning Machine. The goal is not to claim a quantum computational advantage, but to enrich feature representation while preserving the efficiency of lightweight analytical learning. Experiments conducted on the ICBHI 2017 respiratory sound benchmark show that AI-Sono improves a standard ELM baseline while maintaining negligible training overhead. The final results indicate that AI-Sono is not the strongest overall classifier among the evaluated baselines, but remains competitive as a lightweight analytical alternative. In particular, the proposed framework preserves very low training and inference cost, while repeated-run and ablation analyses suggest that the oscillatory enrichment can provide bounded but meaningful gains over a standard ELM pipeline. Overall, AI-Sono should be interpreted as a screening-oriented lightweight benchmark framework for respiratory sound analysis in resource-constrained settings, rather than as a clinically ready diagnostic system.
